Community Engagement Project

Road Safety Mapping Around Schools

We walked the roads around Satish Pradhan Dnyanasadhana College in Thane, recorded what is unsafe for students on foot, and put every risk spot on a map.

Location
Dnyanasadhana College and Teen Haath Naka junction, Thane
Team
Abhijeet Salve, Aditya Salian, Abhinav Pandey
Guide
Prof. Smita Patil
Tool
Google My Maps
Open the risk map See field photos

Section 1

Project description

What the project is, in three short points.

Observe. We visited the college and the nearby junction at busy hours and noted how people cross, how traffic moves, and what safety infrastructure exists.

Record. We took geo-tagged photos of footpaths, crossings, signage and traffic points, so every finding is tied to a real place.

Map and suggest. We turned the findings into a colour-coded digital map with a recommended fix for each spot, and made it easy to share with students and the college.

Section 2

Problem observed

Why we chose this topic and what we found on the ground.

Students face daily risk crossing roads near Dnyansadhana College due to missing crossings, poor signage and unregulated traffic.

  • Broken and blocked footpathsDebris, rubble and cracked slabs push people onto the road.
  • Missing or faded crossingsZebra markings are worn away at one crossing and absent at the junction.
  • Little signageWe saw no school-zone or pedestrian warning boards on the main approach.
  • Heavy, mixed trafficTrucks, autos, buses and bikes share the junction at peak hours.
  • Hazards on the walking pathA loose cable, fallen leaves and a rusted sheet barricade sit on one footpath.
  • Standing water near the flyoverPuddles and a damaged edge make the approach road slippery for walkers.

Section 3

Objectives

What we set out to do.

  1. Find and document the unsafe spots for pedestrians around the college.
  2. Collect real data through observation, photos and conversations with people who use the road.
  3. Rate each spot as caution or danger.
  4. Build a digital risk map with photos and notes on every pin.
  5. Suggest a practical fix for each spot.
  6. Share the map with students, the college and local authorities through one link.

Section 7

Proposed improvements

The real photo on the left, and what the same place could look like with our fixes on the right.

The images marked Proposed concept are AI-generated pictures made to show our recommendations. They are not photos of finished work.

Flyover approach

Clear the clutter, widen and clean the footpath, add a tactile path for visually impaired walkers, cover the drain, and paint a zebra crossing and box junction.

Teen Haath Naka junction

Paint a zebra crossing and yellow box-junction lines so vehicles keep the crossing clear.

Main road crossing

Repaint the zebra crossing and add "Stop for pedestrians" and "Safe crossing for students" signs, with bollards to protect the footpath edge.

Underpass crossing

Add pedestrian signals, a marked crossing and direction signs so people cross together and drivers know to stop.

Broken pavement

Remove the rubble, relay the surface so it is continuous, and keep a railing between the footpath and parked vehicles.

Section 8

Digital risk map

Our main output. Every risk spot is a pin with a photo, a note and a fix.

How to read the map

  • Yellow pin: caution. A real but smaller risk, such as faded markings.
  • Red pin: danger. A serious risk, such as a missing crossing at a busy junction.

The map has separate layers for risk spots and for recommendations, so you can switch between them.

Open the live map

Opens Google My Maps in a new tab. It works on phone and laptop and needs no sign-in to view.

Section 9

Recommendations

What the college and local authorities can do first.

  • Mark a clear crossing at the college gateZebra paint plus "school ahead" and "stop for pedestrians" signs.
  • Repair the flyover footpathsRemove rubble and clutter, relay the surface, cover open drains.
  • Add a crossing and signal at the junctionPedestrian signal, zebra crossing and box-junction lines at Teen Haath Naka.
  • Slow traffic near school hoursSpeed breakers and reduced-speed signs on the approach roads.
  • Station a traffic guard at peak timesMorning arrival and afternoon dismissal at the junction.
  • Keep footpaths clearMove loose cables and barricades, and stop parking on the walking path.
